_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4b, IC4-R1). `pairs` is the plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides. The confused pairings (Ney/Lannes, Massena/Davout) drawn twice each.

who.Ney: Ney — a bold marshal, famous for his courage and his impatience to fight.
who.Davout: Davout — a careful marshal, strict, exact, who counts every man and never wastes one.
who.Murat: Murat — a bold cavalry marshal who loves to ride and charge.
who.Lannes: Lannes — a bold marshal who marches to the sound of the guns and leads assaults himself.
who.Massena: Masséna — a stubborn marshal who never gives up ground he holds.
who.Bernadotte: Bernadotte — a slow, politic marshal who is never in a hurry and always has an excuse.

pairs.line1: Leave it to me, Sire. No more waiting — I'm moving now.
pairs.line2: As I see fit, Sire. Wherever the guns are loudest, that's where you'll find me.

pairs.line1: The job's done, Sire. Point me at the guns.
pairs.line2: It's done, Sire, so what next? I'm no man to sit and admire it.

pairs.line1: I'd keep this ground, Sire. It's mine now, and worth keeping.
pairs.line2: Let me dig in here, Sire, and see every man fed and in his place.

pairs.line1: We won, Sire. I've counted the losses, and I'll allow a little more risk.
pairs.line2: We won, Sire. The field is mine now, and I'll hold it.

pairs.line1: Very well, Sire, but don't leave me idle. Send me at someone soon.
pairs.line2: Recalled? As you wish, Sire — I was in no rush.

pairs.line1: My corps is rested and in no danger.
pairs.line2: I see dust on the roads and none of it worth following.

pairs.line1: No news from my part of the line, Sire. Let's hope it stays that way.
pairs.line2: All in order here, Sire. Every man is in his place.

pairs.line1: Understood, Sire. Where the guns are, I'll be.
pairs.line2: I'll check the rolls and the stores first, Sire. Then I begin.

pairs.line1: I let you down, Sire. Give me a horse and another try.
pairs.line2: I failed, Sire. Straight talk: I'll lead the assault again.

pairs.line1: There, Sire, done, as I said. Now find me something to fight.
pairs.line2: Was that not handsomely ridden, Sire?

pairs.line1: I must say I have doubts, Sire. I'll go, slowly.
pairs.line2: I don't like leaving a place I've made mine, Sire. I'll go if I must.

pairs.line1: Recalled, Sire? The horses and I were enjoying ourselves.
pairs.line2: Recalled, Sire? What I held there was mine, but as you wish.

rows.line: Last time you pulled me off it. Let me finish it now.
Last time I was called back, Sire, no doubt for good reasons. I'd like to finish this one, in my own good time.
You called me back last time, Sire. Let me see this one through.
I was passed over once. I'd rather you checked the rolls to see who is senior.
Last time your order kept my columns from a friend's fight. I remember it.
You gave another man the ground that was mine to take, Sire. I remember it.
We struck out from my front today, Sire.
My corps did its part today, Sire. I'm sure you'll see it's mentioned.
We fought today, Sire. I've been itching for it.
The cavalry was in it today, Sire. You could hear us coming.
The columns went in at the run, Sire. Hot work.
Every man was in place, so I sent them in, Sire.
I said I'd ride it. I rode it with style.
Done, Sire. The columns went in and I never doubted them.
It is done, Sire, and without any fuss. I hope that counts.
It's done, and every yard held. Remember it when someone speaks against me.
Done as promised, Sire. Now let me get back to fighting.
It is done, Sire, and not a man wasted.
Your order first, Sire. My task will keep, and so will my ground.
Your order first, Sire. The guns can hold off a day for me.
As you say. Tomorrow I'm back at it, and no more sitting about.
Your order, Sire. My own chase can wait a day.
Your order first, of course, Sire. My task can wait, and I'm in no rush.
Your order first, Sire. My task is noted and will be resumed with every man in his place.
Let me dig in here, Sire, and see every man fed and in his place.
Let me hold and watch the roads, Sire. The first dust I see, I'm after it.
Let me hold here, Sire, though I can't sit long. The first enemy who shows will regret it.
Leave me here, Sire. This is my ground, and they pay for every yard.
Let me keep this post, Sire. I'm sure you'll agree it's sensible.
I'll hold here with the columns ready, Sire, and my ear on the guns.
